answers.reason: ¶161 review OTC labels for required warnings; the regulatory reference is paraphrased as 'labeling rules' without changing scope (OTC only) or recommended strength.
¶162 control code must identify the finished product with a lot or control number permitting determination of complete manufacture and control history; mandatory.
List item ¶165 under 'Determine:': where package control number differs from batch number, how it relates and identifies the original batch; condition stated.
List item ¶167 gang-printed labels prohibited unless differentiated by size, shape or color; the 'unless' exception is kept and the 1994 effective date has long passed, so mandatory is right.
¶168 'shall' use one of the special controls for cut labels; statement lists all three options from ¶169-¶171 including one-person visual exam independently verified by a second person.
List item ¶172 reconciliation waived for cut or roll labeling if 100-percent examination is performed per regulation; condition kept, optional.
¶175 laboratory controls should include adequate specifications and test procedures for components, in-process and finished products against identity, strength, quality, purity; complete.
List item ¶177 under the ¶176 lab-controls lead-in: master file of specifications for all raw materials used in manufacture; 'all' kept, recommended.
¶177 master file should include sampling procedures, sample size, number of containers, sample identification, tests, and retest dates for deteriorating components; all six elements kept.
¶178 manufacturer responsible for verifying supplier assay protocols by periodic own complete testing and routine identity tests on all raw materials received; both methods kept.
List item ¶179 laboratory procedure for releasing raw materials, finished bulk or packaged drugs from quarantine; all three material types kept.
¶179 determine who is responsible for the quarantine-release decision; statement asks responsibility be assigned, recommended.
¶179 raw material specifications should include approved suppliers; recommended, nothing added.
¶179 for NDA/ANDA drugs, approved suppliers in specifications should match those in the application; condition stated, recommended.
List item ¶180 lab staffed and equipped for all raw material, in-process and finished testing claimed; 'that is claimed' kept.
List item ¶181 if drug preparations are tested during processing, representative sample from various stages; condition stated.
List item ¶182 specifications and description of laboratory testing procedures for finished products; recommended.
List item ¶183 procedures for identity and strength of all actives incl. pyrogen and sterility testing if applicable; 'if applicable' kept.
List item ¶184 where the lab conducts pyrogen, safety tests or bioassays, animals adequately fed and housed; condition kept, the animal count is an inspection datum not an obligation.
¶184 care of lab animals on weekends and holidays, within the animal-testing condition; recommended.
List item ¶185 sterility testing procedures under the ¶176 lab-controls lead-in; INJ only, recommended.
¶186 sterility test entries permanently recorded showing all results positive and negative; 'permanently' and 'all' kept.
List item ¶187 sterility testing facility should be similar to those used for manufacturing products; recommended, INJ.
List item ¶188 laboratory procedures for handling sterile samples, framed under the sterility-testing lead-in of ¶186.
List item ¶191 procedure for identifying test media with specific batches; 'specific batches' kept.
List item ¶192 test media's ability to support growth of organisms; recommended under sterility-testing determinations.
List item ¶194 procedure for diluting products to offset bacteriostatic agents; purpose kept.
¶195 animals from positive pyrogen tests withdrawn from use for the required period; 'required period' kept, INJ.
¶197 if tests are made by outside laboratories, precautions to ensure the work is bona fide; condition stated, recommended.
List item ¶198 methods to check reliability, accuracy and precision of lab procedures and instrumentation; all three attributes kept.
List item ¶200 complete records of all lab test data incl. dates, endorsements of individuals performing tests, and traceability; all kept.
¶201 reserve sample program and procedures for components and finished product; both material types kept, recommended.
¶201 reserve samples maintained and retrievable; both elements kept, recommended.
¶201 reserve sample storage container must maintain product integrity; mandatory.
List item ¶203 under ¶202 'Whether stability tests are performed on:' - drug product in its marketed container-closure system; recommended.
List item ¶204 stability tests on solutions prepared as directed in labeling at time of dispensing; lead-in kept.
¶204 expiration dates based on appropriate stability studies placed on labels; 'appropriate stability studies' kept.
List item ¶205 if penicillin and non-penicillin products share premises, non-penicillin products tested for penicillin; condition stated.
¶208 master production and control records must be prepared per the drug CGMPRs; citation paraphrased, mandatory kept.
¶208 master records may be in several locations but should be readily available for review; recommended, both parts kept.
¶210 batch production and control records must document each significant step in manufacture, labeling, packaging and control of specific batches; all four phases kept, mandatory.
¶210 the several separate records forming a complete production and control record should be readily available to the investigator; recommended.
¶213 batch records specific as to equipment (v-blender vs ribbon blender) and processing times (mixing time and speed); examples kept, recommended.
¶213 equipment should have its own unique identification number; recommended, nothing added.
¶213 manufacturing process must be standardized, controlled and validated; all three requirements kept, mandatory; 'these products' refers to the products whose batch records are discussed.
¶214 complete distribution records should be maintained; 'complete' kept, regulation citation omitted only as a reference, recommended.
¶215 determine whether the firm checks authenticity of orders received; recommended, nothing added.
¶216 regulation requires records of all written and oral complaints be maintained; both complaint types kept, mandatory.
¶217 complaint files should be readily available for review; recommended.
¶217 all complaints handled as complaints and not inappropriately excluded; 'all' and 'inappropriately' kept.
¶218 complaints fully investigated; 'fully' kept, recommended investigator determination.
¶218 appropriate corrective action taken based on investigation conclusions; recommended.
¶222 returned drug items examined in the laboratory and identification of who makes the ultimate decision on their use; both elements kept.
¶223 salvage drugs properly disposed of to preclude salvage; purpose kept, recommended.
¶223 drugs should be disposed of per EPA regulations, paraphrased as environmental protection regulations; recommended.
